https://www.itv.com/news/calendar/2025-0.title: Parole Board recommends 'shoe fetish killer' Christopher Farrow is moved to open prison
https://www.itv.com/news/calendar/2025-0.text:
The Parole Board has recommended that a murderer who was dubbed the "shoe fetish killer" is moved to an open prison.
Christopher Farrow, 61, was given a life sentence in November 2000, with a minimum term of 18 years, for the rape and murder of 51-year-old Wendy Speakes at her home in Wakefield.
Farrow was 33 when he forced his way into Ms Speakes' home in March 1994, tied her up with a pair of stockings and made her wear a pair of blue mule shoes he had brought with him.
He then raped her and stabbed her to death.
Since 2018, when he reached his minimum term, Farrow, from Cookridge in Leeds, has been denied parole three times, most recently in 2023.
He was previously moved to an open prison in 2018 in preparation for release, but was returned to a higher security facility two years later after a challenge.
At a hearing in February 2025, the Parole Board again considered whether he could be released or moved to an open prison.
It heard that Farrow, who is now 63, had undertaken accredited programmes in prison to address his sexual offending as well as one-on-one sessions with a psychologist.
The panel heard he had "developed insight into his risk factors and had gained skills in custody linked to his emotional management and problem solving."
But none of the witnesses who gave evidence to the panel supported him being freed.
In its conclusion, the Parole Board said: "The panel noted that the index offences was a brutal, sexual, and violent attack.
"Although Mr Farrow had completed extensive work in custody to explore his offending behaviour, the panel considered that it was only his recent work that had allowed professionals to say that he had shown insight into his offending.
"Release was not supported by witnesses and the panel was not satisfied that release at this point would be safe for the protection of the public. However, on considering the criteria for recommending placement in open conditions, the panel recommended that Mr Farrow should be progressed in this way."
Farrow's case will be sent to the Justice Secretary Shabana Mahmood MP who will decide whether the move to open prison will go ahead.

https://www.itv.com/news/central/2025-03.title: Birmingham City Council declares major incident over bin strikes
https://www.itv.com/news/central/2025-03.text:
A major incident has been declared by Birmingham City Council after rubbish continues to mount across the city due to the ongoing bin strikes.
The council has said they have a contingency plan using limited resources to collect from all properties in the city once a week - but actions on the picket line have prevented them from doing this.
They estimate that around 17,000 tonnes of waste remains uncollected around the city.
They said the daily blocking of our depots by pickets has meant that they cannot get vehicles out tocollect waste from residents which has meant that around 17,000 tonnes of waste remains uncollected across the city.
The council has outlined by declaring a major incident, they will be able to carry out the following emergency plan:
Quickly increase the availability of street cleansing and fly-tip removal with an additional 35 vehicles and crews around the city.
Work with partners to better manage the risks the city is facing, including health and fire risks and allow for increased data and intelligence sharing.
Allow the council to explore what further support is available from neighbouring authorities and government to assist us in managing the situation.
A focus of the major incident will be on making sure bin lorries can safely enter and exit the council’s waste depots.
The council usually deploy around 200 vehicles over 8-hour daily shifts. Their contingency allows 90 vehicles to operate per day but because of pickets blocking depots they are deployed much later and therefore for shorter working periods.
They would normally make well over 500,000 collections per week. Our strike contingency would mean 360,000 but they say because of depots being blocked that they are  far below this.

“I would reiterate that we have made a fair and reasonable offer to our workers which means none of them have to lose any money and I would urge Unite to reconsider their position.”

There are calls for swifter action against animal cruelty following secret filming at a Warwickshire abattoir, as ITV News Central reporter Pablo Taylor reports...
Residents in a Warwickshire village have been protesting outside of an abattoir after a video was released online showing what they say is evidence of animal abuse.
Australian filmmaker and animal rights activist, Joey Carbstrong, installed secret cameras in a halal slaughterhouse in Arley.
He says he filmed around 200 hours of footage last summer, and claims to have found multiple instances of possible illegality at the abattoir in relation to the rough handling of the animals and ineffective restraints during slaughter.
The footage appears to show sheep and goats being killed and some dismembered whilst still showing signs of life.
Some animals also appear to be forcefully manhandled and hit by workers.
The slaughterhouse, owned by T&S Abattoir, is being investigated by the Food Standards Agency.
Three workers from the slaughterhouse have been fired.
The footage formed the basis of a report by Jenny L. Mace, an associate lecturer at the University of Winchester, who specialises in animal welfare, behaviour, ethics, and law.
Under government regulations, halal slaughterhouses must wait a minimum of 20 seconds after cutting sheep and goats to ensure they have lost consciousness.
But Ms Mace, told ITV News Central that, according to her, that wasn’t happening.  She said: “The staff, the slaughter is supposed to be systematically checking for a lack of consciousness in the sheep.
"It was clear that there were no systematic checks going on for consciousness in the sheep before they were being moved.
"Sometimes it was so blatant that there was consciousness still present because of the extent of movement going on.”

Animal welfare expert Jenny Mace analysed the footage and told ITV News Central that the animals were still conscious when they were slaughtered
The MP for Nuneaton Jodie Gosling raised the issue in the House of Commons saying: "Footage, released yesterday [5th March], appears to show 200 horrific hours of repeated animal abuse at an abattoir in my constituency.
"I have been working with residents and a multitude of agencies to try and ensure safety and compliance long before my election to this place.
"Many now feel outraged that the regulatory systems have failed to notice, let alone address the repeated breaches.
"So I ask the leader of the house if she can work with me to establish why it took an activist to highlight these issues whilst my constituents in Old Arley and these animals continue to suffer.
"And ways to ensure that tighter scrutiny, swifter action, and that when standards are not met, that businesses are closed."
Lucy Powell, Manchester Central MP and Leader of the house, responded saying: "We take a zero tolerance approach to breaches in animal welfare such as those she has described.
"I think the Food Standards Agency has already taken some action, but if they haven't taken some action, I will ensure that they do."

In an interview with ITV News Central, Jodie Gosling MP said the complaints of residents "need to be heard"
The Food Standards Agency (FSA) told ITV News Central:“We are taking this issue seriously. Following a review of this footage, we have already taken action to suspend several individuals from handling live animals while we look into these allegations further.
"We initially received some of the covert footage on Thursday 13 February 2025, although we’ve been told that this filming took place from July and August 2024.
"We had already identified and appropriately enforced animal welfare failures at this establishment prior to being sent the covert footage.
"Since last summer, we’ve put in place increased official presence and have continued to work onsite to ensure improvements were made.
"It would be inappropriate to comment further at this stage as the investigation is ongoing but we will not hesitate to take more action where required as we have a zero-tolerance approach to animal welfare breaches.”
T&S Abattoir, who own the Abattoir, told ITV News Central: "We have taken the necessary action and terminated contracts of those thought to be involved as this goes completely against our values and animal welfare policies.
"We are assisting relevant authorities in their enquiries. This footage is thought to have been taken in July 2024, soon after we started operating from the site.
"Continual improvements have been made since that time.
"This includes increasing the frequency of monitoring, adding CCTV cameras to cover what were previously blind spots, improvement of restraining equipment and infrastructure, incorporating a 20+ second timer, retraining current staff on our animal welfare policy and introducing more experienced management to oversee operations all to ensure that our animal welfare policy is always adhered to."

DCI David Andrews from Warwickshire Police said: “Following our visit on Monday 3 March, we are working with partners including the Home Office and Food Standards Agency to take appropriate action regarding the issues identified.
“Since our visit, and in light of the footage shared by the Independent, which we believe was filmed in July 2024, we can confirm that we have recorded a suspected offence of unnecessary suffering to a protected animal under animal welfare legislation.
"While this investigation into animal welfare is underway, we cannot go into further detail about the case so that we do not jeopardise any future proceedings.”
Inspector Andi Gibbons from the North Warwickshire Safer Neighbourhood Team (SNT) said,
"Our safer neighbourhood officers will continue to engage with the community and we wish to reassure you that these matters are being dealt with. If you do have concerns, please reach out to our team".

https://www.itv.com/news/calendar/2025-0.title: A63 stabbing trial: Girl attacked with sword during Hull camping trip, court told
https://www.itv.com/news/calendar/2025-0.text:
A 13-year-old girl was attacked with a sword after a falling out during a friends' camping trip, a court has heard.
The victim was stabbed 10 times by a 14-year-old boy who offered to walk her home after a disagreement with another girl near Hull, a jury at Hull Crown Court was told.
She suffered injuries to her head, neck, chest, back and arms, but managed to stagger to the side of the A63, close to the Humber Bridge, where she was seen trying to flag down passing motorists.
The boy, who cannot be named due to his age, is charged with attempted murder. His trial is expected to last four days.
Prosecutor David Lamb KC described how the two teenagers were in a group of seven young people who walked through Hessle to camp near the Humber Bridge.
One of them had a kortada sword, similar to a Samurai sword, when they pitched a tent on grassland to the rear of the Humber View Hotel in Hessle.
After a disagreement, the court was told, the victim asked to leave. The boy offered to walk her through woods between the grassland and the A63.
Mr Lamb said the boy asked the girl to stop while he urinated in the woods, but then removed the sword that he had secreted in his waistband.
He added: “He pushed her to the ground to start with before he crouched down and said ‘I’m sorry, I have to do this’.”
The court was told the boy restrained her, grabbing her by her neck, and stabbed her 10 times, causing cuts, a collapsed lung and a damaged liver.
The attack only stopped when she managed to kick him away.
The court was shown dashcam footage of the victim waving down traffic on the A63 while covered in blood, as well as police bodycam footage of the defendant’s arrest after being removed from a tent.
Mr Lamb said: “The attack was sustained, it was determined, it was constant and conducted with a weapon we say was used with the obvious intent to kill that young girl.”
Police found the sword in the defendant's tent. Forensic analysis showed both the weapon and a jacket worn by the defendant had traces of the victim's blood.
The court heard how the defendant initially denied stabbing the victim before telling his legal team five days after the attack that he was responsible.
He claimed another member of the group had given him £20 to carry out the attack following the argument.
The defendant has already pleaded guilty to wounding with intent and possessing the sword but denies attempted murder. The trial continues.

https://www.itv.com/news/calendar/2025-0.title: Reform mayoral campaign launch disrupted by anti-racism protesters
https://www.itv.com/news/calendar/2025-0.text:
Nigel Farage was repeatedly heckled by anti-racism protesters during a speech announcing Reform UK’s candidate for the Doncaster mayoral election.
The party leader was speaking for less than a minute before a succession of demonstrators interrupted his speech at the event in South Yorkshire on Tuesday.
Mr Farage began his speech by vowing his party would “stun the establishment” at the May local elections. Reform says it will stand candidates in every seat on the ballot.
Shortly afterwards, eight students and activists stood up to accuse Reform of racism.
“Farage offers nothing for ordinary people”, the Stand Up To Racism group, with which the protesters were affiliated, said.
One of the demonstrators shouted “free Palestine!” before being escorted out of the venue.
As they were led away, the party leader described one as a “saddo” and another as a “loser”.
“We will not be stopped by a ranting student mob, we will fight on and win these elections in Doncaster,” he told audience members.
“Go back to school please, we know what’s going to happen. Boring, boring, boring. They will do everything they can to stop this being a free and fair election.”
He added: “That’s what you get folks, when teaching unions in this country are poisoning the minds of young people, not just against Reform, but against everything this country has ever stood for.
“I’ll make it clear, when we’re in a position of power, we will go to war with these left-wing teaching unions and make sure our kids are taught properly.
“The point about our country is, in a democracy, you can disagree with people, but in a democracy you respect the right of other people to have different opinions, to express them.”
The party leader had been speaking at the launch of the election campaign of Alexander Jones, Reform UK’s candidate for the Doncaster mayoralty.
Mr Jones, described by the party as having worked in property “before founding his own Forex trading business and modelling”, said he would help to unlock the “broken” city’s potential.
“Growing up in Doncaster showed me how our communities can be forgotten and failed by politicians who promise much but deliver little.
“Doncaster has huge potential, and I am confident that I can unlock it and deliver the opportunities and investment local people deserve,” he said.
“A vote for Labour or the Conservatives in this election is a vote for more of the same complacency and decay that has held Doncaster back for years. Doncaster is broken. Reform will fix it.”
Sabby Dhalu, co-convener of Stand Up To Racism, said the group had challenged Mr Farage because he and his party were “trying to spread hate and division at a time when we need unity”.
Weyman Bennett, another co-convener, said: “Reform claims to stand for ordinary people, but its real agenda is one of division and distraction. Farage is a millionaire banker who does not represent working-class interests.”

'Obviously something has gone wrong in your life': The moment Mohammad Farooq was arrested
A former student nurse who plotted a terrorist attack on the hospital where he had worked has been jailed for a minimum of 37 years.
Mohammad Farooq took a home-made pressure cooker bomb into St James's Hospital in Leeds in January 2023, but “lost his bottle” after talking to a patient.
Prosecutors said the clinical support worker had planned to “kill as many nurses as possible” by targeting the maternity wing.
Farooq, 29, was jailed for life with a minimum 37-year term.
Sheffield Crown Court heard how Farooq targeted the hospital as his “plan B” after first travelling to the American base at RAF Menwith Hill, in North Yorkshire, but failing to get past security.
During a three-week trial the jury heard he was a "self-radicalised lone wolf" inspired by Daesh propaganda to procure weapons and manufacture an explosive device.
His "secondary motive" was a grievance held against several former colleagues who he had been conducting a poison pen campaign against, the court was told.
He planned to "seek his own martyrdom" through a "murderous terrorist attack" before using an imitation firearm to incite police to shoot him dead.
The bomb he developed was modelled on those detonated at the 2013 Boston Marathon but had twice the amount of explosives.
Some of the hospital's wards were evacuated after reports of a suspicious package.
The plot stalled after Farooq was talked down by patient Nathan Newby, who saw him outside the hospital's Gledhow Wing.
Farooq had already pleaded guilty to possessing an explosive substance with intent to endanger life, firearms offences and the possession of terrorist material.
The judge, Mrs Justice Cheema-Grubb, praised the actions of Mr Newby, saying: “He’s an extraordinary, ordinary man whose decency and kindness on 20 January 2023 prevented an atrocity in a maternity wing of a major British hospital.”
She said Mr Newby was a “modest and gentle man whose evidence was among the most remarkable this court has ever heard”.
The judge told Farooq: “This was deliberately to cause maximum damage to life. But at the end, your courage failed you and the kind thoughtfulness of a passing stranger saved you and those you targeted.”
She said: “You were prepared to do the unthinkable. To explode a bomb in a hospital. Your responsibility is not reduced by the fact that you lost your bottle and were persuaded, while in emotional turmoil, to stand down and let Mr Newby call the police.”
Det Supt Paul Greenwood, head of investigations for Counter Terrorism Policing North East, said: "Farooq came dangerously close to harming innocent people.
"Thanks to the bravery of Nathan Newby he never fully realised his plans and has instead been forced to face the long-term consequences of his extreme ideology and deep-seated grievances."
Prof Phil Wood, chief executive of Leeds Teaching Hospitals NHS Trust, said the sentencing would help staff to "continue to move on".
He added: "It was an extremely difficult time for staff and patients, and I remain immensely proud of the calm and professional way in which they responded on the day to keep everyone safe.
“I would again like to thank the police for their support during the incident and throughout the investigation, and I am extremely grateful to Nathan Newby for his courage and initiative that morning.”

https://www.itv.com/news/calendar/2025-0.title: Brothers jailed 18 years after raping girls in Rotherham
https://www.itv.com/news/calendar/2025-0.text:
Two brothers who raped vulnerable girls have been given lengthy prison sentences.
Mark Evans, 37, and Robert Evans, 40, abused children in Rotherham over a two-year period starting in 2006.
The pair, aged 18 and 21 at the time, intimidated girls and plied them with drugs and alcohol before luring them to locations where they attacked them, the National Crime Agency said.
The brothers were arrested in August 2020 after officers from the NCA’s Operation Stovewood, examining historic sexual abuse in Rotherham, investigated allegations made by three victims.
Two of the women subsequently told specialist investigators they were raped by both brothers.
One of them was 13 at the time. She was given alcohol by Mark Evans before she and some friends accompanied
him to a disused barn. He then separated her from her friends and raped her.
The same woman was attacked by Robert Evans several months later, when he lured the girl to a house in Rotherham by lying that one of her friends would be there.
Robert Evans plied her with alcohol as they took a bus to the house. Once Evans had the victim alone at the house,
he raped her. She recalled he seemed amused by this.
Another woman said she too was raped by both brothers when she was 14. She knew the men because they spent time with other girls her age.
She recounted how Mark Evans walked her home one evening because it was dark, but as they passed through an alleyway he raped her.
She and the first victim were later lured by Robert Evans to a house, on a separate occasion to when the first victim was attacked by him. At the house, Robert Evans forced the second girl into a bathroom and raped her.
The third victim was age 13 when Mark Evans began grooming her by giving her alcohol and drugs, and calling her his “girlfriend”.
The victim told officers how Mark Evans visited her at her home and asked her for sex. Fearing Evans would break up with her, she went to an alleyway where he had sex with her.
The brothers were found guilty of a number of sexual offences, including rape, following a trial at Sheffield Crown Court.
Mark Evans was jailed for 14 years. Robert Evans was given a 17-year sentence.
NCA senior investigator Kim Boreham said: “I would like to recognise the courage and strength of the three victims in this case. For almost 20 years these women have suffered the profound consequences of Mark and Robert Evans’ crimes, while the two men continued their lives as normal."
Samantha Thompson, of the Crown Prosecution Service said: “The Evans brothers targeted and groomed young girls including with alcohol and drugs, for child sexual abuse and rape.
“The lifelong physical and emotional trauma caused to victims by men like the Evans brothers cannot be understated. This type of conduct has equally damaged the community confidence of Rotherham.
“We would like to thank the victims in this case for coming forward and reporting this devastating crime."

https://www.itv.com/news/central/2025-03.title: Birmingham bin strikes: Council refuse workers begin indefinite strike amid row over jobs and pay
https://www.itv.com/news/central/2025-03.text:
Nearly 400 council bin workers in Birmingham have walked out indefinitely as part of an escalating dispute over jobs and pay.
The Unite union has warned bin disruption in the city could stretch into the summer after refuse workers voted in favour of extending their strike mandate over the council’s use of temporary labour to "undermine” their industrial action.
Unite said its members face pay cuts after the scrapping of waste collection and recycling officer roles, despite already voluntarily accepting cuts to pay and terms and conditions after the council declared bankruptcy.
The union’s national lead officer, Onay Kasab, said: "The council could end this dispute tomorrow by agreeing to pay a decent rate of pay.
"The council is forcing dedicated workers on to pay levels barely above the minimum wage while undertaking a difficult and highly demanding job in all weathers.
"The council could easily afford this if it stopped wasting millions on expensive employment agency fees.
"Disruption to Birmingham’s refuse service will further deteriorate but this is the fault of a heartless council which has slashed pay without a thought to the effect it is having on workers and their families.”
In a statement issued to ITV Central, Birmingham City Council said that they would be open to negotiate with bin workers and the union.
It said: "Our door is always open to Unite and we would encourage them to come back to the table. The further escalation of strike action is causing more misery to residents at even more cost to the taxpayer.”
Birmingham City Council boss Craig Cooper spoke to ITV News Central, saying bin workers who would've had a pay cut were offered other jobs and options, and 80% accepted:
